title: How Indian Consulting Firms Can Receive Card Payments From International Clients in 2026: 3 Collection Workflows Compared
summary: Indian consulting firms can receive card payments from international clients through an approved international payment gateway, using a payment link, hosted
body_markdown:
**Indian consulting firms can receive card payments from international clients through an approved international payment gateway, using a payment link, hosted invoice or recurring subscription.** The client pays in a supported currency; the provider processes the card payment and settles the proceeds into the firm’s Indian bank account under its agreed terms.


For an eligible Indian consultancy,[Razorpay International Payments](https://razorpay.com/accept-international-payments/) is worth evaluating when the business needs project invoices, milestone collections and recurring retainers alongside domestic billing. Start with Payment Links for individual invoices, assess Subscriptions for agreed recurring charges, and offer international bank transfer when the client’s procurement process or the cost comparison favours it.


## Key Takeaways


- Indian consulting firms can receive card payments from international clients using Razorpay Payment Links or Invoices after international-card activation. Eligible Subscriptions can collect recurring retainers. The client pays in a supported currency, and the consultancy receives settlement in its Indian bank account under the approved account terms.
- **Project deposits and milestones:** Share a hosted Payment Link against the agreed invoice. No checkout integration is needed; business verification, website requirements, and international-card approval still apply.
- **Monthly retainers:** Use an eligible subscription with the client’s authorisation, or send a fresh invoice and payment link each month.
- **Bank-transfer alternative:** Offer international bank transfer when it fits the client’s procurement process. Keep its pricing and settlement terms separate from the card option.
- **Compare the full cost:** Check card-processing fees, GST on fees, conversion, any subscription charges and the applicable settlement schedule before choosing a provider.
- **Reconcile every receipt:** Match the invoice, payment and bank credit; use the correct service purpose code and retain the applicable inward-remittance statement.


## Which International Payment Workflow Fits Your Consulting Invoice?


Choose the workflow around how the client pays and how you bill. A recurring invoice does not automatically require an automatic card debit, and a bank-transfer account does not itself provide card acceptance.

The first two are card-collection workflows. The third gives the client a choice between bank transfer and card; the bank-transfer payment itself is not a card transaction.


## Workflow 1: Receive International Card Payments Through a Payment Link


A payment link suits consulting firms that send an invoice after agreeing a scope of work.[Razorpay Payment Links](https://razorpay.com/payment-links/) can be created in the Dashboard and shared by email, without building a checkout integration. International currency support is documented for both dashboard-created and API-created links.


### How to Collect a Project Deposit or Milestone Payment


1. Complete Razorpay account verification and request international-card activation. Provide the business, service and website information requested during review.
2. Agree the invoice amount, currency, deliverable, payment deadline and refund or cancellation terms with the overseas client.
3. Create a Payment Link in a supported currency. Add an identifiable invoice or milestone reference and the client’s genuine contact details.
4. Send the invoice and its matching link to the authorised payer. Ask the client to check whether their corporate card allows the amount and overseas purchase.
5. The client completes the hosted checkout and any issuer-required authentication. Check the payment status in the Dashboard before treating the invoice as collected.
6. Reconcile the payment, processing fee, taxes, conversion and bank settlement against the invoice. Retain the relevant inward-remittance statement.


For a project with three agreed milestones, use an invoice reference for each milestone so finance can reconcile each receipt. Where appropriate, Payment Links also support partial-payment settings, expiry dates and reminders. See the[Payment Links documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/payment-links/) for the supported controls.


### Do You Need a Website to Accept International Cards?


**A hosted Payment Link removes the need to build a checkout, but it does not waive international-card activation requirements.** Razorpay’s[international-card documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/international-payments/international-debit-credit-cards/) requires a KYC-verified account and a valid website with terms, privacy, refund/cancellation and shipping-policy sections. For a consulting service, confirm the appropriate service-delivery policy with the activation team.


Banking-partner approval and security checks apply. Do not promise a client that their card will work before activation, card coverage and the transaction amount have been confirmed.


> **Did You Know?** A payment page and a business website serve different purposes: one collects the payment, while the other helps establish the business and its customer policies during onboarding.


## Workflow 2: Collect Monthly Consulting Retainers With Subscriptions


[Razorpay Subscriptions](https://razorpay.com/subscriptions/) can support scheduled recurring card payments in supported international currencies. It is a useful option for a retainer with clear consent, billing frequency, service scope and cancellation terms.


For variable fees or work that requires a fresh purchase order each month, a new invoice and Payment Link may fit better. Recurring collection should follow the contract and the client’s approval process.


### Set Up a Retainer Without Losing Billing Control


1. Confirm international-card activation, recurring-card support and the intended billing currency for your account.
2. Agree the amount, frequency, start date, duration and cancellation terms in the engagement contract.
3. Create the plan and subscription, and have the authorised cardholder complete the approval process.
4. Track successful and failed charges; assign a finance owner to review billing notifications.
5. For a failed charge, follow the documented retry or recovery process and contact the client when action is required.
6. Reconcile each collected cycle against its invoice and retain the service-delivery and remittance records.


The[Subscriptions FAQs](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/faqs/) distinguish international-card recurring payments from domestic-card rules. They also state that international subscription settlements are in INR. Do not assume domestic UPI mandate rules describe a foreign-issued card.


### Budget for Subscription Fees Separately


Recurring billing can carry an additional product fee. Razorpay’s[pricing explainer](https://razorpay.com/blog/razorpay-payment-gateway-pricing-explained/) lists a 0.99% subscription fee in addition to the underlying payment-method fee, with applicable GST. Confirm the current account quote before agreeing a retainer price.


> **Pro-Tip:** Ask for two quotes for the same monthly engagement: a manually paid card invoice and an authorised recurring-card subscription. Compare the full fee stack against the administrative work each option saves.


## Workflow 3: Offer International Bank Transfer With a Card Fallback


If the overseas client’s accounts-payable team prefers a bank transfer, evaluate[Razorpay International Bank Transfer](https://razorpay.com/accept-international-payments/bank-transfers/) . The product provides approved receiving-account details for supported local bank-transfer and SWIFT flows, with INR settlement to the Indian business.


This gives the consultancy a bank-transfer option within Razorpay’s international-payments offering. Keep a separate international card Payment Link available when the client prefers a card and the transaction is eligible.


### Keep Card and Bank-Transfer Terms Separate


The bank-transfer page lists a 1% fee and zero FX markup for the standard local-account transfer route, with GST applicable and a ₹1,000 flat fee on transactions below ₹1,00,000. Confirm the covered route and fee treatment in your quote. The same page lists US FlashLinks, an ACH-debit product, separately at 2%; it is not an international-card Payment Link.


The[bank-transfer documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/international-payments/international-bank-transfer/) describes T+1 settlement for push-based transfers from payment capture or submission of invoice details, whichever is later. Client-to-receiving-account transit time is additional; ACH debit has a different timeline.


1. Activate the required bank-transfer product and confirm the available currency, rail and receiving-account details.
2. Send the invoice with its payment reference and the correct bank instructions.
3. If you offer a card alternative, make clear that the client should use one route only.
4. Upload the required invoice and buyer information and monitor the actual payment status.
5. When payment is confirmed, close or cancel any unused collection link and reconcile the net credit.


For an invoice outside the provider’s approved limits, ask the provider and your Authorised Dealer bank for an appropriate collection route. Do not split a payment merely to bypass a limit.


## What Does Razorpay Charge for International Consulting Payments?


Razorpay’s[international product page](https://razorpay.com/international/) displays a standard 3% platform fee for international credit cards and payment methods. Its pricing explainer specifies 3% plus GST for international credit and debit cards. Use this as a published reference, then confirm the rate and conversion terms approved for your consultancy.


Cost component What to check


International-card processing Published 3% reference; confirm your approved rate, eligible card types and fee base.


GST on provider fees The pricing explainer specifies 18% on the fee. This is separate from the GST treatment of your consulting invoice.


Currency conversion Confirm the conversion rate, timestamp and any applicable conversion or partner-bank charges. Do not apply bank-transfer zero-FX-markup claims to card payments.


Recurring billing Check the additional subscription fee rather than assuming a recurring charge costs the same as a one-off payment.


Other events Ask about refund treatment, disputes, optional services and any account-specific charges.


### Worked Example: A USD 5,000 Consulting Invoice


Assume an illustrative conversion rate of ₹88 per US dollar and a 3% card-processing fee. These assumptions are for arithmetic only; ₹88 is not a live exchange-rate quote.


Calculation Amount


USD 5,000 × ₹88 ₹4,40,000 gross converted value


3% processing fee ₹13,200


18% GST on ₹13,200 ₹2,376


Balance after these two deductions ₹4,24,424


The processing fee plus GST equals 3.54% of the assumed gross value. This is **not a guaranteed all-in cost or settlement quote** : conversion differences, subscription fees and other applicable charges can change the final amount. Ask every provider to quote the net INR for the same invoice, currency and payment rail.


### When Will the Card Payment Reach Your Indian Bank Account?


Razorpay’s[settlement documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/settlements/) states a default international settlement cycle of **T+7 working days** , with T being the payment-capture date. INR settlement uses the conversion rate at payment creation. Confirm the schedule applicable to your account; a successful card payment is not the same as money already available in your bank.


## What Documents and Purpose Code Does a Consulting Firm Need?


Keep the engagement contract, invoice, client details, payment confirmation, settlement report and relevant inward-remittance document together. The service description and purpose code should reflect the work actually delivered.


### Management Consulting and Software Consulting Use Different Codes


The RBI purpose-code list identifies P1006 for business and management consultancy and public-relations services. It identifies P0802 for software consultancy or implementation other than services covered by the SOFTEX form. A firm calling itself a consultancy does not make P1006 correct for every engagement.


For mixed or specialist services, confirm the classification with your Authorised Dealer bank and provider. Razorpay’s[purpose-code guidance](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/international-payments/purpose-codes) explains how to select and update the code.


### Download the Right Inward-Remittance Statement


For international payments, Razorpay documents downloadable **Foreign Inward Remittance Statements (FIRS)** in the Dashboard. Update the purpose code, then open Account & Settings and select Foreign inward remittance statement under international payment settings.


The[FIRS guide](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/international-payments/firs-automated-process) describes bank-provided certificates and Razorpay-generated statements based on monthly transactions. It also provides a request option when a bank certificate is unavailable or a consolidated statement is needed. Confirm which document your accountant or bank needs for the collection route; FIRS, FIRA and FIRC should not be treated as identical documents.


> **Did You Know?** Your client invoice, payment confirmation, bank settlement and remittance statement answer different accounting questions. Keeping them linked by invoice and payment reference makes a short bank credit easier to reconcile.


### Check Current Export and GST Requirements


The RBI’s consolidated 2026 export regulations, amended through 2 November 2026, generally specify nine months from the invoice date for service-export realisation, with a twelve-month provision for exports invoiced or settled in INR. Exceptions and Authorised Dealer extensions apply. Confirm the provision relevant to your receipt; INR credited after conversion is not, by itself, a reason to assume the longer period applies.


The rules also contain service-export declaration requirements and deemed-submission provisions, including for resident individuals and qualifying receipts of up to ₹10 lakh for other persons. Confirm the applicable process with your Authorised Dealer bank.


Card acceptance does not automatically establish GST export eligibility. Ask your tax adviser to check the place of supply, recipient, payment conditions and the applicable LUT or tax-payment route. Avoid treating a missed 1 April date as an automatic loss of LUT eligibility: CBIC guidance provides for case-specific condonation of delayed LUT filing.


## How Should You Compare Providers for International Consulting Payments?


Choose a provider against the requirements of your actual invoice, rather than a single advertised fee. For a consultancy evaluating Razorpay, ask these questions before the first collection:


- **Business eligibility:** Is your entity and exact consulting activity approved for international cards?
- **Client payment:** Is the client’s card network, issuing country, currency and invoice amount supported?
- **Billing fit:** Can you use a link for each milestone, and is recurring card collection approved when needed?
- **Net receipt:** What reaches the Indian bank after fees, GST, conversion and optional services?
- **Cash flow:** What event starts the settlement clock, and what is your actual account schedule?
- **Records:** Which remittance document can you obtain, and how does it reconcile to the invoice?


Razorpay is a practical candidate when you want international Payment Links, optional recurring billing and a separate bank-transfer route within its product offering. The choice remains conditional on eligibility, the account quote and your client’s payment needs.


### Handle Card Declines and Consulting Disputes


If a card fails, inspect the actual failure reason before asking the client to retry. Check genuine contact and billing information, international-card activation and issuer restrictions. Razorpay documents 3D Secure 2.0 and Address Verification System support; neither guarantees approval of every foreign corporate card.


Keep the signed scope, delivery records, milestone acceptance and client correspondence for dispute handling. A successful payment does not remove chargeback exposure.


> **Pro-Tip:** Before requesting a retainer payment, confirm who owns the corporate card and who approves the invoice. Send both parties the agreed scope and billing terms so an unfamiliar statement descriptor does not create avoidable confusion.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Can an Indian consulting firm accept USD, EUR or GBP card payments?


Yes, subject to international-card approval and the supported currency and card combination. Razorpay documents international currencies for Payment Links and other payment products. Confirm availability for your account before quoting a currency to the client.


### Can an individual consultant use the same international-card workflow?


Do not assume the same eligibility. Razorpay’s international-payments documentation distinguishes registered-business card acceptance from individual collection options. Confirm your business constitution and approved collection route during onboarding.


### Does a Payment Link automatically charge a monthly retainer?


A standard payment link collects a payment when the client pays it. Scheduled recurring collection requires an eligible subscription setup and the customer’s authorisation. Alternatively, send a new invoice and link each month.


### Is the international bank-transfer rate also the card-payment rate?


No. International bank transfers and international cards are separate payment methods with different pricing, settlement and approval conditions. A zero-FX-markup statement for a bank-transfer product should not be applied to card acceptance.


### What should I do after the client pays?


Verify the payment status, match it to the invoice, track the bank settlement, record fees and taxes separately, and retain the applicable remittance statement and service-delivery records.


To evaluate the right setup for your consultancy, review[Razorpay International Payments](https://razorpay.com/accept-international-payments/) and confirm your entity, services, billing currency, invoice values and preferred collection workflow during activation.
